AGENDA
  CITY COUNCIL
  JUNE 6, 2023

UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE, MEETINGS WILL BE CONDUCTED PURSUANT TO THE PROVISIONS OF ASSEMBLY BILL 361,
WHICH ALLOWS COUNCIL MEMBERS TO PARTICIPATE FROM A REMOTE LOCATION WITHOUT LISTING A PHYSICAL
LOCATION. TO PROVIDE COMMENTS DURING A MEETING: YOU MAY ATTEND THE MEETING, SEND AN EMAIL TO:
publiccomments@norwalkca.gov, OR JOIN THE ZOOM MEETING BY CALLING: (669) 900-6833 OR USING THE ZOOM APP
WITH THE FOLLOWING LINK: https://us02web.zoom.us/j/7095732685; MEETING ID: 709 573 2685. THE MEETING MAY BE
VIEWED THROUGH ZOOM, FIOS CHANNEL 32 OR CHARTER CHANNEL 3, OR ON THE CITY'S WEBPAGE AT:
https://www.norwalk.org/city-hall/meeting-agendas-393.

  CLOSED SESSION MEETING
  5:00 PM

  REGULAR MEETING
  6:00 PM
  NORWALK CITY HALL/COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  AND VIA VIDEOCONFERENCE

  Ana Valencia, Mayor
  Margarita L. Rios, Vice Mayor
  Tony Ayala, Councilmember
  Jennifer Perez, Councilmember
  Rick Ramirez, Councilmember

 Public Comment: The public is encouraged to address City Council on any matter listed on the agenda or on any other matter within its
 jurisdiction subject to the rules of decorum described in Section 2.08.020 of the Norwalk Municipal Code. If you wish to address City
 Council, please complete the card that is provided at the rear entrance to Council Chambers and hand the card to the Sergeant at Arms.
 City Council will hear public comment on items listed on the agenda during discussion of the matter and prior to a vote. City Council will
 hear public comment on matters not listed on the agenda during the Oral Communications period.

 Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless certain emergency
 or special circumstances exist. The City Council may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain matters for consideration at a
 future City Council meeting.

 Please adhere to the following procedures when addressing the City Council:
   Comments should be limited to 3 minutes or less.
   Comments should be directed to the City Council as a whole and not directed to individual Councilmembers.

 Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a City meeting or other
 services offered by this City, please contact the City Clerk’s department, (562) 929-5720. Assisted listening devices are available at this
 meeting. Ask the City Clerk if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the agenda and documents in the agenda packet can be
 made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability. Notification of at least 48 hours prior to the meeting or time
 when services are needed will assist the City staff in assuring that reasonable arrangements can be made to provide accessibility to the
 meeting or service.

 Note: Any writings and/or documents provided to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after it has been posted will also
 be made available for public inspection.

 Writings and/or documents are available for inspection in the City Clerk’s Department, City Hall, 12700 Norwalk Boulevard during regular business
 hours, 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday – Thursday and 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., every other Friday; telephone (562) 929-5720. You may also contact the
 City Clerk via e-mail at recordsrequests@norwalkca.gov.
   CLOSED SESSION MEETING – 5:00 PM

CLOSED SESSION REPORT

CITY COUNCIL COMMENTS

a.  Report of City Council Travel

SPECIAL PRESENTATIONS – None.

CITY MANAGER COMMENTS

1.  Mayor’s Prayer Breakfast video.

2.  Memorial Day Ceremony video.

3.  Fireworks Safety Video.

4.  Bi-Weekly Review video.

 CONSENT CALENDAR

 Consent calendar items are considered routine matters which may be enacted by one motion and roll call
 vote. Any item may be removed from the consent calendar and considered separately by City Council.

1.  MEETING MINUTES
  Staff recommends City Council approve the minutes of the meeting of May 16, 2023. 825-04

2.  PAYROLL FOR THE PERIOD APRIL 30, 2023 – MAY 13, 2023 AND MAY 14, 2023 – MAY 27, 2023
  Staff recommends City Council approve:
  a. gross payroll in the amount of $1,131,929.66; the payroll check number 37808-37811 and
  the voucher numbers 318612 – 319068 in the total net amount of $839,561.12 for the pay
  period April 30, 2023 – May 13, 2023.
  b. gross payroll in the amount of $1,102,869.95; the payroll check numbers 37812-37814 and
  the voucher numbers 319069 – 319528 in the total net amount of $822,782.58 for the pay
  period May 14, 2023 – May 27, 2023.
3.  COMMERCIAL DEMANDS
  Staff recommends City Council approve the warrant register period May 9, 2023 through May 22, 2023, in
  the total amount of $2,841,005.67. 640

4.  CLAIMS AGAINST THE CITY
  Staff recommends City Council deny the claim filed by Catherine Allain, Florentina Falcon, Sandra Garcia,
  Mercury Insurance on behalf of Ayanna Smith, Hedy Peng, William Shelly, Shaniece Starnes, and Joshua
  Stockton.

5.  PLANNING COMMISSION SYNOPSIS - MAY 31, 2023
  No action is required unless the City Council elects to review the decision of the Planning Commission on
  the items where the Commission’s action was final.

6.  RESOLUTION NO. 23-28 - STATEMENT OF INVESTMENT POLICY

 City Council, June 6, 2023  Page 3 of 5
   Staff recommends City Council adopt Resolution No. 23-28, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY
  COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NORWALK, ADOPTING THE 2023/24 STATEMENT OF
  INVESTMENT POLICY AND AUTHORIZING THE CITY TREASURER TO INVEST AND
  REINVEST IDLE MONIES OF THE CITY OF NORWALK IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE 2023/24
  STATEMENT OF INVESTMENT POLICY.

7.  RESOLUTION 23-29 – ADOPTING PURCHASING POLICY FOR FISCAL YEAR 2023/24
  Staff recommends City Council adopt Resolution No. 23-29, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF
  THE CITY OF NORWALK ADOPTING THE PURCHASING POLICY FOR FISCAL YEAR 2023/24.

8.  AGREEMENT AMENDMENT NO. 5 - PRODUCTION OF THE CITY’S MONTHLY NEWSLETTER
  PUBLICATION (NORWALK NOW)
  Staff recommends City Council approve Amendment No. 5 with Norwalk Printing Co. Inc., in the amount of
  $25,920 from July 1, 2023 through August 31, 2023 for the printing of the City's newsletter publication; the
  maximum compensation set forth is a sum not to exceed Six Thousand Four Hundred and Eighty Dollars
  ($6,480.00) (“the maximum compensation”) per month; and authorize the City Manager to execute the
  amendment on behalf of the City, in a form approved by the City Attorney.

9.  AGREEMENTS FOR MAJOR BUS COMPONENTS AND MAJOR REPAIR SERVICES FOR NORWALK
  TRANSIT SYSTEM
  Staff recommends City Council approve a three year agreement, from July 1, 2023 through June 30, 2026
  with Cummins, Inc. for $80,000; Gillig, LLC for $50,000; and Western States Converters and Transmissions,
  Inc. for $25,000, for a total of $155,000 for Fiscal Year 2023/24 for Major Bus Components and Major
  Repairs and an option to extend the agreements for two one-year periods for a total contract value of
  $465,000; and authorize the City Manager to execute the agreements, and any amendments provided there
  is funding in the budget and it is within the City Manager’s signing authority, on behalf of the City, in a form
  approved by the City Attorney.

10. AGREEMENT - EMERGENCY OPERATIONS CENTER AUDIO/VISUAL EQUIPMENT
  Staff recommends City Council approve an agreement with One Diversified, LLC for Emergency Operations
  Center Audio/Visual Equipment in an amount not-to-exceed $295,927.88; and authorize the City Manager
  to execute the agreement and any amendments, provided there is funding in the budget and it is within the
  City Manager’s signing authority, on behalf of the City, in a form approved by the City Attorney.

11. PROJECT NO. 7928.1 – AGREEMENT AMENDMENT NO. 1 - CONSTRUCTION AND CONSTRUCTION
  SUPPORT SERVICES FOR LOCAL STREETS REHABILITATION PROGRAM PHASE 2 - ZONE 8,
  ENGINEER’S REPORT NO. 23-06
  Staff recommends City Council approve Amendment No. 1 with CJ Concrete Construction adding $301,922
  to Project No. 7928; and authorize the City Manager to execute the amendment, provided there is funding
  in the budget, on behalf of the City, in a form approved by the City Attorney.

12. PROJECT NO. 7927.1 – AGREEMENT AMENDMENTS - CONSTRUCTION AND CONSTRUCTION
  SUPPORT SERVICES FOR LOCAL STREETS REHABILITATION PROGRAM – PHASE 2 ZONE 3,
  ENGINEER’S REPORT NO. 23-05
  Staff recommends City Council:
  a. approve Amendment No. 1 to the agreement with CJ Concrete Construction in the amount of
  $495,825 for Project No. 7927; and authorize the City Manager to execute the amendment, provided
  there is funding in the budget, on behalf of the City, in a form approved by the City Attorney; and
  b. approve Amendment No. 3 to the agreement with Onward Engineering in the amount of $25,000 for
  Project No. 7929; and authorize the City Manager to execute the amendment, provided there is
  funding in the budget, on behalf of the City, in a form approved by the City Attorney.

13. PROJECT NO. 1.7C4219 WEBSITE ENHANCEMENTS - WEBSITE DESIGN SERVICES AND CONTENT
  MANAGEMENT SYSTEM

 City Council, June 6, 2023  Page 4 of 5
   Staff recommends City Council award a contract to Revize Software Systems for website design services
  and content management system upgrades in an amount not to exceed $50,000; and authorize the City
  Manager to execute the contract and any amendments provided there is funding in the budget and it is
  within the City Manager’s signing authority, on behalf of the City, in a form approved by the City Attorney.

APPOINTMENTS

14. ADVISORY BODY APPOINTMENTS
  Staff recommends City Councilmembers make appointments to fill the vacancies on the various Advisory
  Bodies for two-year terms expiring on December 31, 2024.

ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS

15. URGENCY ORDINANCE NO. 23-1740U AMENDING CHAPTER 10.20 OF THE NORWALK
  MUNICIPAL CODE AND REVISING THE DESIGNATED TRUCK ROUTE
  Staff recommends City Council:

  a. Find that the adoption of the Urgency Ordinance is exempt from the California Environmental
  Quality Act pursuant to the following: CEQA Guidelines Section 15601(b)(3) as it will not result
  in a direct or indirect physical change or significant effect on the environment, and CEQA
  Guidelines Section 15378(b)(5) as an administrative activity of the government that will not result
  in a direct or indirect physical change to the environment; and because the Urgency Ordinance
  relates to existing streets and does not approve a specific project within the City, none of the
  exceptions to categorical exemptions under CEQA Guidelines Section 15300.2 apply.
  b. adopt Urgency Ordinance No. 23-1740U, AMENDING CHAPTER 10.20 OF THE NORWALK
  MUNICIPAL CODE AND REVISING THE DESIGNATED TRUCK ROUTE AND ASSOCIATED
  REGULATIONS, AND DETERMINING THAT THE ORDINANCE IS EXEMPT FROM REVIEW
  UNDER THE CALIFORNIA ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY ACT, and waive full reading.

REPORTS

16. PARK PROJECTS UPDATE
  Receive and file.

17. 2023 STRATEGIC PLAN
  Staff recommends City Council approve the 2023 Strategic Plan.

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

ADJOURNMENT

I hereby certify under penalty of perjury under the laws of the State of California that the foregoing agenda was
posted on the City Hall bulletin board not less than 72 hours prior to the meeting. Dated June 2, 2023.

Theresa Devoy, CMC
City Clerk

 City Council, June 6, 2023  Page 5 of 5
